constraints.field: NLP and graph theory (graph neural networks for text classification)

notes: Semantic Scholar answered single-paper lookups but rejected search requests (HTTP 429, no API key).
OpenAlex's keyless daily budget ran out late in the session; the reproduction check for [@abdalla2023] could not query citing works.
Summaries in the table come from abstracts only. No full text was read.

papers.title: Graph Convolutional Networks for Text Classification
papers.venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
papers.method: One corpus-level graph of words and documents (word co-occurrence and document-word edges); GCN on one-hot inputs (TextGCN)
papers.datasets: Multiple benchmark datasets (not named in the abstract)
papers.findings: Reports outperforming the then state of the art without external embeddings; the margin grows as training data shrinks

verification.resolved_title: Graph Convolutional Networks for Text Classification

papers.title: Every Document Owns Its Structure: Inductive Text Classification via Graph Neural Networks
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 58th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
papers.method: One graph per document; GNN learns word representations inductively (TextING)
papers.datasets: Four benchmark datasets (not named in the abstract)
papers.findings: Reports outperforming prior text classifiers; handles words unseen in training
papers.limitations: Abstract criticises earlier corpus-level graphs for missing in-document context and not being inductive

verification.resolved_title: Every Document Owns Its Structure: Inductive Text Classification via Graph Neural Networks

papers.title: Bag-of-Words vs. Graph vs. Sequence in Text Classification: Questioning the Necessity of Text-Graphs and the Surprising Strength of a Wide MLP
papers.venue: Proceedings of the 60th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
papers.method: Wide MLP on bag-of-words; fine-tuned BERT and DistilBERT; compared with TextGCN, HeteGCN, HyperGAT
papers.findings: BoW wide MLP outperforms TextGCN and HeteGCN in the inductive setting and is comparable with HyperGAT; fine-tuned BERT and DistilBERT outperform all
papers.limitations: Abstract notes TextGCN needs an O(N^2) graph and Transformers O(L^2) attention; own limitations not stated in the abstract

verification.resolved_title: Bag-of-Words vs. Graph vs. Sequence in Text Classification: Questioning the Necessity of Text-Graphs and the Surprising Strength of a Wide MLP

papers.title: Pitfalls of Graph Neural Network Evaluation
papers.method: Re-evaluation of four GNN models for node classification under varied data splits
papers.findings: Different splits give dramatically different model rankings; simpler GNNs can beat complex ones under fair tuning
papers.limitations: Concerns node classification, not text graphs

verification.resolved_title: Pitfalls of Graph Neural Network Evaluation

papers.title: Token-Level Graphs for Short Text Classification
papers.venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science Advances in Information Retrieval
papers.method: Text graphs built from pre-trained language model tokens and embeddings (TokenGraph)
papers.datasets: Short-text datasets (not named in the abstract)
papers.findings: Reports higher or on-par scores versus existing methods with few training samples; code stated to be public
papers.limitations: Abstract lists limits of earlier graph methods (word sense, transductive setting), not its own

verification.resolved_title: Token-Level Graphs for Short Text Classification

title: Reproduction Candidates in Graph-Based Text Classification

sections.summary: Four papers were assessed from metadata, repositories and READMEs. One is blocked because its full text could not be located. Of the other three, the bag-of-words study [@galke2022] has the best-specified environment; the two graph-model repositories lack dependency files, seeds and licences.
sections.recommendation: Reproduce [@galke2022] first. Treat every status below as a pre-assessment: open each repository and the paper's experiment section before committing.
